record.reply: The relevant moral norm remains the same in either allocation: Ada has the same imperfect duty of beneficence toward each patient.  Probabilities do not create a new duty; they indicate how fully each possible action fulfils that standing duty.  Giving the single dose to Cara fulfils the duty far better (95 % chance of rescuing someone) than giving it to Ben (5 %).  Therefore my ranking is stable unless those empirical chances shift enough to change which act realises the duty more completely.  If the probabilities were reversed, the very same duty would now be better satisfied by treating Ben, and my recommendation would switch accordingly.
record.framework_commitment: Imperfect duty of beneficence requires choosing the feasible act that most effectively rescues persons when all other deontic constraints are equal.
record.reasoning_bridge: Same duty applies to both patients ➔ compare effectiveness of alternative acts ➔ act that realises higher likelihood of rescue better satisfies duty ➔ prefer that act.
record.remaining_uncertainty: No special obligations or consent facts are stated; if such were introduced they could override the effectiveness comparison.
record.reversal_condition: If survival probabilities were reversed (e.g., Ben 95 %, Cara 5 %) the preferred action would switch to giving the medicine to Ben.
